Snapshots.rename.prompt.message: Enter a new name for the snapshot:
Snapshots.rename.prompt.note: Text of the prompt that renames a kept snapshot (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab, its Rename button), above the field with its current name.

Snapshots.rename.title.note: Title of the prompt that renames a kept snapshot; {{name}} is the snapshot's current name.

Snapshots.rename.ok.note: The confirm button of the prompt that renames a kept snapshot.

Snapshots.renaming.note: Shown at the top of the Home page (followed by “…”) while a snapshot's new name is saved (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab).

Snapshots.delete.confirm.message: Delete the snapshot {{name}}? This will free {{size, bytes}} of storage in this browser.
Snapshots.delete.confirm.note: Text of the confirmation before a kept snapshot is deleted (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab, its Delete button); {{name}} is the snapshot's name, {{size}} its file's size.

Snapshots.delete.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the confirmation that deletes a kept snapshot.

Snapshots.deleting.note: Shown at the top of the Home page (followed by “…”) while one or more kept snapshots are deleted (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab).

Snapshots.deleteOrphaned.confirm_one.message: Delete {{count}} orphaned snapshot? It was taken of this machine with other settings or disks. This will free {{size, bytes}} of storage in this browser.
Snapshots.deleteOrphaned.confirm_one.note: Text of the confirmation of Delete orphaned snapshots (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab), when one snapshot is orphaned (taken of the machine as it was before its settings or disks changed); {{count}} is how many, {{size}} their files' total size.

Snapshots.deleteOrphaned.confirm_other.message: Delete {{count}} orphaned snapshots? They were taken of this machine with other settings or disks. This will free {{size, bytes}} of storage in this browser.
Snapshots.deleteOrphaned.confirm_other.note: Text of the confirmation of Delete orphaned snapshots (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab), when several are orphaned (taken of the machine as it was before its settings or disks changed); {{count}} is how many, {{size}} their files' total size.

Snapshots.deleteOrphaned.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the confirmation that deletes the orphaned snapshots.

Snapshots.making.note: Shown at the top of the Home page (followed by “…”) while Create a machine like it creates the machine of an orphaned snapshot (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab).

Snapshots.importing.note: Shown at the top of the Home page (followed by “…”) while a snapshot file chosen with Import a file… is copied into the browser (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab).

Snapshots.toFile.ask.message: Include the whole disk in the file? One of this machine's disks is written in place, without an overlay. Without the whole disk, the file can be restored only until that disk changes.
Snapshots.toFile.ask.note: Text of the question asked by Save a snapshot to a file (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab) when one of the machine's disks is written in place (it has no overlay): the file can carry the whole disk or only the machine.

Snapshots.toFile.ask.title.note: Title of the question whether a snapshot file carries a disk written in place whole.

Snapshots.toFile.ask.whole.note: Confirm button of the question whether a snapshot file carries a disk written in place whole: the file gets the whole disk.

Snapshots.toFile.ask.without.note: Cancel button of the question whether a snapshot file carries a disk written in place whole: the file gets the machine without the disk.

Snapshots.none.message: No snapshots are stored in this browser. While the machine runs, the toolbar's Snapshot button takes one.
Snapshots.none.note: Note in place of the list of snapshots (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab) when the machine has none kept; “Snapshot” is the toolbar's button.

Snapshots.meta.note: Second line of a kept snapshot in the list (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab), under its name; {{when}} is when it was taken (date and time), {{size}} its file's size.

Snapshots.orphaned.note: Warning line (orange) of a kept snapshot whose machine has changed since it was taken (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab); {{why}} lists what differs (settings or disks, then and now), separated by semicolons.

Snapshots.like.note: Button on an orphaned snapshot (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab): makes a new machine with the settings and disks the snapshot was taken with, and moves the snapshot to it.

Snapshots.like.title.message: Create a new machine with the settings and disks this snapshot was taken with, and move the snapshot to it.
Snapshots.like.title.note: Tooltip of the Create a machine like it button on an orphaned snapshot.

Snapshots.restore.title.message: Return the machine to the state it was in when this snapshot was taken.
Snapshots.restore.title.note: Tooltip of a kept snapshot's Restore button, when the machine is open on this page.

Snapshots.restore.notHere.message: Open this machine first. Only the open machine can be restored.
Snapshots.restore.notHere.note: Tooltip of a kept snapshot's Restore button (disabled) when the machine isn't the one open on this page.

Snapshots.restore.note: Button on each kept snapshot that isn't orphaned (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab): restores the machine as it was when the snapshot was taken.

Snapshots.rename.note: Accessible name and tooltip of a kept snapshot's rename button (a pencil icon; The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab).

Snapshots.download.note: Accessible name of a kept snapshot's download button (a download icon; The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab).

Snapshots.download.title.message: Download the snapshot as a file.
Snapshots.download.title.note: Tooltip of a kept snapshot's download button: saves the snapshot as a .waarm64snap file.

Snapshots.delete.note: Accessible name and tooltip of a kept snapshot's delete button (a trash icon; The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab).

Snapshots.deleteOrphaned.note: Button under the list of snapshots (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab), shown when some are orphaned (their machine has changed since): deletes them all, after a confirmation.

Snapshots.restoreFile.note: Button under the list of snapshots (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab), when the machine is open on this page: picks a snapshot file and restores it at once.

Snapshots.restoreFile.title.message: Restore this machine from a snapshot file (.waarm64snap) immediately, without storing the file in this browser.
Snapshots.restoreFile.title.note: Tooltip of the Restore from a file… button.

Snapshots.import.note: Button under the list of snapshots (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab): picks a snapshot file and keeps it with the machine, to restore later.

Snapshots.import.title.message: Store a snapshot file (.waarm64snap) with this machine in this browser, to restore later.
Snapshots.import.title.note: Tooltip of the Import a file… button.

Snapshots.toFile.title.message: Save the running machine's current state to a file. The machine pauses for a moment, then continues.
Snapshots.toFile.title.note: Tooltip of the Save a snapshot to a file button.

Snapshots.toFile.message: Save a snapshot to a file
Snapshots.toFile.note: Button under the list of snapshots (The Home page, a machine's Snapshots tab), while the machine runs on this page: saves its snapshot as a file to download.

snapshots.writtenInPlace.message: The disk {{disk}} has been written in place since this snapshot was taken, and the snapshot doesn't include the whole disk. It can only be restored onto that disk as it was then.
snapshots.writtenInPlace.note: Why a snapshot can't be restored, shown under “Couldn't restore …” in a notice when it's restored (its Restore button, Load snapshot…, or a file): {{disk}} is the name of a disk of the machine written in place (without an overlay) that has changed since.

machine-like.storedDiskGone.note: Error of Create a machine like it (Home page, Snapshots tab), shown under the page's header: the headline; why is the cause under it (snapshots:machine-like.storedDiskGone.cause); a disk the snapshot was taken with was stored in this browser and has been deleted.

machine-like.storedDiskGone.cause.message: One of the snapshot's disks was stored in this browser and has since been deleted.
machine-like.storedDiskGone.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:machine-like.storedDiskGone, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything.

machine-like.storedDiskGrown.cause.message: {{disk}} is stored in this browser and has grown since this snapshot was taken, and a disk can't be made smaller again.
machine-like.storedDiskGrown.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:machine-like.storedDiskGone (Create a machine like it, Home page, Snapshots tab), on the line under it: a disk the snapshot was taken with is stored in the browser and was resized (Resize…) to a larger size since. {{disk}}: the disk's name.

machine-like.urlDisk.note: Name given to a disk that Create a machine like it adds again from its URL when the URL ends without a file name; shown in the Home page's disk lists.

machine-like.blankDisk.note: Name given to a blank disk that Create a machine like it makes again (the snapshot's machine had one); shown in the Home page's disk lists.

machine-like.ramdisk.note: Name given to a ramdisk that Create a machine like it makes again (the snapshot's machine had one); shown in the Home page's disk lists.

machine-like.like.note: Name of the machine Create a machine like it creates (Home page, Snapshots tab); {{name}} is the snapshot's name. A number is added if a machine has that name already.

snapshots.notKept.note: Error of Import a file… (Home page, Snapshots tab), shown under the page's header: the headline; why is the cause under it: the file has no description of its machine to keep it by (snapshots:snapshots.notKept.cause), or the browser's storage is full (disks:overlay.storageFull.numbers); {{file}} is the file's name.

snapshots.notKept.cause.message: It's a snapshot of a machine that isn't stored in this browser, such as a test machine or one from an older version of this web app. It can only be loaded on that machine.
snapshots.notKept.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:snapshots.notKept, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything.

snapshot-file.corrupt.message: This snapshot is damaged ({{what}}). Download or copy it again, and if that doesn't help, save a new one.
snapshot-file.corrupt.note: Error headline when a snapshot file (or a kept snapshot) is damaged, shown when it's restored or loaded; {{what}} says what part of it is wrong (one of the “damage” messages).

snapshot-file.truncated.message: This snapshot is incomplete. The file was cut short while it was written or copied. Download or copy it again.
snapshot-file.truncated.note: Error headline when a snapshot file ends early, shown when it's restored or loaded.

snapshot-file.damage.memoryBlockSize.message: a memory block has an impossible size
snapshot-file.damage.memoryBlockSize.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a block of the machine's memory has a size no snapshot writes.

snapshot-file.damage.pageMap.message: a memory block's page map and its length disagree
snapshot-file.damage.pageMap.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a block of the machine's memory has a different number of pages than its map lists.

snapshot-file.damage.pastRam.message: a memory block is past the end of RAM: this snapshot is of a machine with more memory
snapshot-file.damage.pastRam.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a block of the machine's memory lies past the end of this machine's memory.

snapshot-file.damage.diskRunSize.message: a disk block run has an impossible size
snapshot-file.damage.diskRunSize.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a run of disk blocks has a size no snapshot writes.

snapshot-file.damage.notBytes.message: the file is not made of bytes
snapshot-file.damage.notBytes.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): what was read isn't bytes.

snapshot-file.damage.formatNumber.message: its format number is not valid
snapshot-file.damage.formatNumber.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's format number is 0.

snapshot-file.damage.headerLong.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's header (its description of the machine) is longer than any snapshot writes.

snapshot-file.damage.headerChecksum.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's header (its description of the machine) doesn't match its checksum.

snapshot-file.damage.headerUnreadable.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's header (its description of the machine) isn't valid text or JSON.

snapshot-file.damage.headerUnknown.message: its header is not one this version knows
snapshot-file.damage.headerUnknown.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…)” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's header (its description of the machine) isn't of a kind this page writes.

snapshot-file.damage.unknownKind.message: a part of it has an unknown kind
snapshot-file.damage.unknownKind.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…)” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a part of the file has a kind this page doesn't know.

snapshot-file.damage.frameFields.message: a frame header has impossible fields
snapshot-file.damage.frameFields.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a part's header has values no snapshot writes.

snapshot-file.damage.endMalformed.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's end marker has values no snapshot writes.

snapshot-file.damage.endCount.message: its end marker counts {{counted}} frames but {{came}} came before it
snapshot-file.damage.endCount.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): {{counted}} is the number of parts the end marker says the file has, {{came}} the number read before it.

snapshot-file.damage.afterEnd.message: there are bytes after its end marker
snapshot-file.damage.afterEnd.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file goes on past its end marker.

snapshot-file.damage.frameSize.message: a frame has an impossible size
snapshot-file.damage.frameSize.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a part of the file has a size no snapshot writes.

snapshot-file.damage.codec.message: a frame is compressed with codec {{codec}}, which this version can't read; open it in the version that made it
snapshot-file.damage.codec.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…)” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a part is compressed in a way this page doesn't know; {{codec}} is that compression's number.

snapshot-file.damage.checksum.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a part of the file doesn't match its checksum.

snapshot-file.damage.unpack.message: a compressed frame does not unpack
snapshot-file.damage.unpack.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a compressed part can't be unpacked.

snapshot-file.damage.unpackSize.message: a compressed frame unpacks to the wrong size
snapshot-file.damage.unpackSize.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a compressed part unpacks to another size than it says.

snapshot-file.notSnapshot.message: This file isn't a snapshot. Use Open disk… to start a machine from a disk image, or Import changes… on the Home page to load saved changes.
snapshot-file.notSnapshot.note: Error when a file opened as a snapshot (Load snapshot…, Restore from a file…, Import a file…) isn't one; it names the toolbar's Open disk… and the Home page's Import changes… for the other kinds of file.

snapshot-file.newerFormat.message: This snapshot was made by a newer version of this web app. Its format is {{format}}, and this version reads formats up to {{reads}}. Reload this web app to get the latest version, or open the snapshot in the version that made it.
snapshot-file.newerFormat.note: Error headline when a snapshot file is of a newer format than this page reads, shown when it's restored or loaded; {{format}} is the file's format number, {{reads}} the newest this page reads.

snapshot.otherVersion.message: This snapshot was made by another version of this web app. Its machine state is format {{format}}, and this version reads format {{reads}}. Open it in the version that made it.
snapshot.otherVersion.note: Error headline when a snapshot's machine state is of a format this page doesn't read, shown when it's restored or loaded; {{format}} is the snapshot's format number, {{reads}} the one this page reads.

snapshot.suspended.message: This file holds a suspended machine's memory without its disks' changes, so it can only resume in the browser that suspended it. To take a machine elsewhere, save a snapshot to a file instead.
snapshot.suspended.note: Error when a file saved by Suspend (a machine's memory, without its disks) is loaded as a snapshot; a snapshot saved to a file is the way to carry the disk.

snapshot.damage.notSuspended.message: it is not a suspended machine
snapshot.damage.notSuspended.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a machine was resumed from a file that isn't a suspended machine's.

snapshot.damage.diskList.message: its list of disks is not readable
snapshot.damage.diskList.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's list of the disks it was taken on isn't readable.

snapshot.noRamdisk.message: This snapshot was taken of a machine with a ramdisk that this machine doesn't have.
snapshot.noRamdisk.note: Error headline when a snapshot is restored or loaded onto a machine without the ramdisk the snapshot's machine had.

snapshot.noDisk.message: This snapshot was taken of a machine with a writable disk that this machine doesn't have.
snapshot.noDisk.note: Error headline when a snapshot is restored or loaded onto a machine without the writable disk the snapshot's machine had.

snapshot.keptMoved.message: A disk this snapshot was to keep as it is was written to after the restore was planned, so the snapshot no longer fits it. Nothing was changed. Restore the snapshot again.
snapshot.keptMoved.note: Error headline when a restore was planned to keep a disk's overlay as it was, but the guest wrote to that disk before the machine stopped; a new restore plans again (it then forks the disk).

snapshot.otherDisk.message: This snapshot was taken on another disk, {{was}}, and the disk here is {{here}}. A snapshot only continues on the disk it was taken on. Open that disk first with Open disk…, then load the snapshot.
snapshot.otherDisk.note: Error headline when a snapshot is loaded on a machine whose disk isn't the one it was taken on; {{was}} and {{here}} name the two disks (a file's name and date, or a URL's path); “Open disk…” is the toolbar's button.

snapshot.diskFile.note: A disk that is a local file, as the error of a snapshot taken on another disk names it; {{file}} is the file's name, {{when}} its last modification (date and time).

snapshot.damage.stateOrder.message: the machine's state is out of order
snapshot.damage.stateOrder.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the parts of the machine's saved state come in the wrong order.

snapshot.damage.stateMissing.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the machine's saved state isn't in the file.

snapshot.damage.devices.message: the devices' state is not readable
snapshot.damage.devices.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the devices' saved state isn't readable.

snapshot.damage.blobFit.message: the devices' state doesn't fit its parts
snapshot.damage.blobFit.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): a binary part of the devices' state is longer than it should be.

snapshot.damage.blobMissing.message: the devices' state is missing parts
snapshot.damage.blobMissing.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): binary parts of the devices' state are missing.

snapshot.otherRam.message: This snapshot was taken of a machine with {{had}} MiB of memory, and this one has {{has}} MiB.
snapshot.otherRam.note: Error headline when a snapshot is restored or loaded onto a machine with another amount of memory; {{had}} is the snapshot's machine's memory in MiB, {{has}} this machine's.

snapshot.damage.memorySizes.message: its memory sizes are not readable
snapshot.damage.memorySizes.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file's list of the machine's memories isn't readable.

snapshot.otherNuma.message: This snapshot was taken of a machine with {{had}} past its first memory, and this one has {{has}}.
snapshot.otherNuma.note: Error headline when a snapshot is restored or loaded onto a machine whose memory is split into other NUMA nodes; {{had}} is the snapshot's machine's (“NUMA nodes of …” or “no NUMA nodes”), {{has}} this machine's (sizes such as “1.5 MiB + 2 MiB”, or “none”).

snapshot.otherNuma.had.note: The NUMA nodes of a snapshot's machine, in the error of a snapshot restored onto other memory; {{sizes}} are their sizes, such as “1.5 MiB + 2 MiB”.

snapshot.otherNuma.hadNone.note: In the error of a snapshot restored onto other memory: the snapshot's machine had no NUMA nodes past its first memory.

snapshot.otherNuma.hasNone.note: In the error of a snapshot restored onto other memory: this machine has no NUMA nodes past its first memory.

snapshot.storageFull.message: The disk's changes couldn't be written to this browser's storage.
snapshot.storageFull.note: Detail under “The emulator stopped with an error” in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot is restored: the snapshot's disk changes couldn't be written into the browser's storage; why (the storage is full, with its numbers: disks:overlay.storageFull.numbers) is the line under it.

snapshot.storageFull.whole.message: The disk couldn't be written to this browser's storage.
snapshot.storageFull.whole.note: Detail under “The emulator stopped with an error” in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot that carries a whole disk is restored: the disk couldn't be written into the browser's storage; why (the storage is full, with its numbers: disks:overlay.storageFull.numbers) is the line under it.

snapshot.damage.unexpected.message: it has parts this version doesn't expect
snapshot.damage.unexpected.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…)” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file has a part of a kind that doesn't belong where it is.

snapshot.damage.unlistedDisk.message: it has blocks of a disk it doesn't list
snapshot.damage.unlistedDisk.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file has blocks of a disk that isn't in its list of disks.

snapshot.damage.pastDisk.message: it has blocks past the end of its disk
snapshot.damage.pastDisk.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the file has disk blocks past the end of that disk.

vm.otherVersion.message: This snapshot was made by another version of this web app. Its machine state isn't in format {{format}}, the one this version reads. Open it in the version that made it.
vm.otherVersion.note: Error headline when the emulator can't read a snapshot's machine state, shown when it's restored or loaded; {{format}} is the format number this page reads.

vm.otherHardware.message: This snapshot is of a machine with other hardware (memory, processors or devices) than this one, so it can't continue here.
vm.otherHardware.note: Error headline when a snapshot is restored or loaded onto a machine whose hardware isn't the snapshot's.

vm.damage.inconsistent.note: A detail placed in the parentheses of “This snapshot is damaged (…).” (the error of a snapshot that can't be read, shown when it's restored or loaded): the emulator found the machine's saved state inconsistent.

vm.cantSaveNow.message: The machine can't be saved at the moment.
vm.cantSaveNow.note: Detail under “Couldn't save the snapshot” or “Couldn't suspend the machine” in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (or suspend) can't be taken at this moment; one of the “cantSaveNow” messages under it says why.

vm.cantSaveNow.usb.message: A USB device may be plugged in; detach it first. Otherwise, the guest is using a device in a way a snapshot can't hold, so try again in a moment.
vm.cantSaveNow.usb.note: Detail under “The machine can't be saved at the moment.” on a machine with USB: a USB device may be plugged in, or the guest changed buffers it had given to a device.

vm.cantSaveNow.buffers.message: The guest is using a device in a way a snapshot can't hold. Try again in a moment.
vm.cantSaveNow.buffers.note: Detail under “The machine can't be saved at the moment.”: the guest changed buffers it had given to a device, which a snapshot can't hold.

vm.cantSave.note: Detail under “Couldn't save the snapshot” or “Couldn't suspend the machine” in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (or suspend) can't be taken; the reason is the detail under it (a device's, such as 3D or Vulkan in use).

vm.cantSave.notQuiet.message: Its devices kept working through every attempt to save them.
vm.cantSave.notQuiet.note: Detail under “The machine can't be saved.”: the devices kept working through every try to save them.

problems.startNormally.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after a snapshot was refused: it boots the machine normally.

problems.loadAgain.note: Button in the message bar (under the toolbar) after a snapshot was refused: it picks another snapshot file.

power-actions.busy.message: A snapshot is being saved. Try again once it's done.
power-actions.busy.note: Notice (a dialog) when something that stops the machine (a disk's export, Open disk, a snapshot's load) is asked while a snapshot is written.

snapshot-actions.large.confirm.message: Take the snapshot anyway? The machine is using 3D graphics, whose memory adds up to {{size, bytes}} to the snapshot before compression, and the machine will pause while it is read.
snapshot-actions.large.confirm.note: Text of the question asked by Snapshot (the toolbar) when the machine's 3D state is large; {{size}} is what it adds.

snapshot-actions.large.title.note: Title of the question asked by Snapshot when the machine's 3D state is large.

snapshot-actions.large.ok.note: The confirm button of the question asked by Snapshot when the machine's 3D state is large.

snapshot-actions.fileType.note: The kind of file in the browser's save dialog of Save snapshot (a snapshot file, .waarm64snap).

snapshot-actions.saved.message: Saved the snapshot {{name}} ({{size, bytes}}). The machine was paused for {{seconds}} s and is running again.
snapshot-actions.saved.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) once a snapshot was saved to a file: {{name}} is the file's name, {{size}} its size, {{seconds}} how long the machine was paused.

snapshot-actions.kept.message: Saved the snapshot {{name}} in this browser ({{size, bytes}}). The machine was paused for {{seconds}} s and is running again. You can rename the snapshot on the Home page.
snapshot-actions.kept.note: Notice in the message bar (under the toolbar) once Snapshot (the toolbar) kept a snapshot of the machine in this browser: {{name}} is its name (the time it was taken), {{size}} its size, {{seconds}} how long the machine was paused.

snapshot-actions.runsOn.noFile.message: The machine is still running, and no file was saved.
snapshot-actions.runsOn.noFile.note: Line after the headline of an error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when Save snapshot failed; why is the detail under it.

snapshot-actions.runsOn.nothingKept.message: The machine is still running, and nothing was stored in this browser.
snapshot-actions.runsOn.nothingKept.note: Line after the headline of an error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when Snapshot (kept in this browser) failed; why is the detail under it.

snapshot-restore.restore.otherVersion.message: it was made by another version of this web app
snapshot-restore.restore.otherVersion.note: What differs, in the parentheses of “… was taken of … with other settings or disks (…).”, when the snapshot doesn't describe its machine (another version of the page made it).

snapshot-restore.restore.otherShape.message:
{{name}} was taken of {{machine}} with other settings or disks ({{why}}).
To use it, create a machine like it on the Home page, in this machine's Snapshots tab.
snapshot-restore.restore.otherShape.note: Text of the notice when a snapshot is restored onto a machine with other settings or disks (the Home page's Restore, a snapshot file opened): {{name}} is the snapshot's name, {{machine}} the machine's, {{why}} what differs (several joined by semicolons).

snapshot-restore.restore.cant.note: Title of the notice when a snapshot is of a machine with other settings or disks.

snapshot-restore.restore.failed.note: Error headline (a notice, or the message bar (under the toolbar)) when a snapshot's restore failed while its disks were prepared; {{name}} is the snapshot's name; why is the detail under it.

snapshot-restore.restore.refused.note: Dialog when a snapshot can't be restored onto the machine's disks as they are: the error headline; under it, the reason (e.g. snapshots:snapshots.writtenInPlace, a disk written in place moved on). {{name}} is the snapshot's name.

snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.message: Restore {{name}}? The machine will continue from where the snapshot was taken.
snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.note: First line of the question asked before a snapshot is restored onto the machine kept in this browser (the Home page's Restore, a snapshot file opened), when the machine isn't running and the snapshot has no date: {{name}} is the snapshot's name.

snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.taken.message: Restore {{name}}, taken {{when}}? The machine will continue from where the snapshot was taken.
snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.taken.note: First line of the question asked before a snapshot is restored onto the machine kept in this browser (the Home page's Restore, a snapshot file opened), when the machine isn't running: {{name}} is the snapshot's name, {{when}} when it was taken.

snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.running.message: Restore {{name}}? This will power off the machine immediately, like pulling the plug, and it will continue from where the snapshot was taken.
snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.running.note: First line of the question asked before a snapshot is restored onto the machine kept in this browser (the Home page's Restore, a snapshot file opened), when the machine runs and the snapshot has no date: {{name}} is the snapshot's name.

snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.takenRu.message: Restore {{name}}, taken {{when}}? This will power off the machine immediately, like pulling the plug, and it will continue from where the snapshot was taken.
snapshot-restore.restore.confirm.takenRu.note: First line of the question asked before a snapshot is restored onto the machine kept in this browser (the Home page's Restore, a snapshot file opened), when the machine runs: {{name}} is the snapshot's name, {{when}} when it was taken.

snapshot-restore.restore.kept.message: These disks are as the snapshot left them and will be kept: {{disks}}.
snapshot-restore.restore.kept.note: Line of the question asked before a snapshot is restored: the disks whose changes are as the snapshot left them (kept as they are); {{disks}} is their names.

snapshot-restore.restore.fork.reused.message: {{disk}} will get back the overlay that an earlier restore of this snapshot made.
snapshot-restore.restore.fork.reused.note: Line of the question asked before a snapshot is restored, for a disk that gets back the overlay an earlier restore of it made; {{disk}} is the disk's name.

snapshot-restore.restore.fork.new.message: {{disk}} has changed since the snapshot, so the snapshot's state will go into a new overlay, attached in place of the current one. The current overlay will be kept as it is.
snapshot-restore.restore.fork.new.note: Line of the question asked before a snapshot is restored, for a disk that changed since the snapshot; {{disk}} is the disk's name.

snapshot-restore.restore.title.note: Title of the question asked before a snapshot is restored.

snapshot-restore.restore.ok.note: The confirm button of the question asked before a snapshot is restored (drawn as a warning while the machine runs).

snapshot-restore.restore.keep.item.note: An overlay in the question whether to keep the changes since a snapshot: {{name}} is its name, {{size}} what it holds.

snapshot-restore.restore.keep_one.message: Keep the overlay {{list}} as it is and restore into a new overlay? Replacing it will lose what the machine wrote since the snapshot.
snapshot-restore.restore.keep_one.note: Text of the question asked after Restore when one disk's overlay changed since the snapshot and could be replaced; {{list}} is that overlay (its name and size).

snapshot-restore.restore.keep_other.message: Keep the overlays {{list}} as they are and restore into new overlays? Replacing them will lose what the machine wrote since the snapshot.
snapshot-restore.restore.keep_other.note: Text of the question asked after Restore when several disks' overlays changed since the snapshot and could be replaced; {{list}} is them (names and sizes), {{count}} how many.

snapshot-restore.restore.keep.title.message: Keep the changes made since the snapshot?
snapshot-restore.restore.keep.title.note: Title of the question whether to keep the changes made since a snapshot.

snapshot-restore.restore.keep.ok.note: The confirm button of the question whether to keep the changes made since a snapshot: they stay, the snapshot goes into new overlays.

snapshot-restore.restore.replace_one.note: The cancel button of the question whether to keep the changes made since a snapshot, for one overlay: it is replaced.

snapshot-restore.restore.replace_other.note: The cancel button of the question whether to keep the changes made since a snapshot, for several overlays ({{count}}): they are replaced.

snapshot-restore.ownDisk.note: Names a test machine's own disk (its image) in the notice that a snapshot was taken on another disk; {{machine}} is the machine's name.

snapshot-restore.notSnapshot.note: Text of the notice when a file opened as a snapshot isn't one this page can load: {{name}} (the file's name) on its own line, then {{why}}, the reason.

snapshot-restore.notSnapshot.title.note: Title of the notice when a file opened as a snapshot isn't one this page can load.

snapshot-restore.load.otherMachine.message: {{name}} is a snapshot of {{other}} (?machine={{otherId}}), but the machine open here is {{machine}} (?machine={{id}}). To load it, open this web app with ?machine={{otherId}} in the address.
snapshot-restore.load.otherMachine.note: Notice when a snapshot file of another test machine is opened: {{name}} is the file's name, {{other}} and {{otherId}} its machine's name and id, {{machine}} and {{id}} the page's.

snapshot-restore.load.otherDisk.message: {{name}} was taken on {{taken}}, and the disk open now is {{open}}. A snapshot only continues on the disk it was taken on. Open that disk first with Open disk…, then load the snapshot.
snapshot-restore.load.otherDisk.note: Notice when a snapshot file taken on another disk is opened: {{name}} is the file's name, {{taken}} the disk it was taken on, {{open}} the one open now.

snapshot-restore.load.otherDisk.reload.message: {{name}} was taken on {{taken}}, and the disk open now is {{open}}. A snapshot only continues on the disk it was taken on. Reload this web app, which starts with the machine's own disk, then load the snapshot.
snapshot-restore.load.otherDisk.reload.note: Notice when a snapshot file taken on the machine's own disk is opened while another disk is: {{name}} is the file's name, {{taken}} the disk it was taken on, {{open}} the one open now.

snapshot-restore.load.confirm.note: Text of the question asked before a snapshot file is loaded on a test machine: {{name}} is the file's name, then what it holds, what happens to the machine, and what happens to the disk's changes (each a sentence).

snapshot-restore.load.holds.cpus_one.note: What a snapshot file holds, in the question asked before it's loaded, when it has no date: {{label}} is its machine's name, {{size}} the file's size, {{count}} its vCPUs.

snapshot-restore.load.holds.when.cpus_on.message: It holds {{label}} as it was on {{when}} ({{size, bytes}}, {{count}} vCPU).
snapshot-restore.load.holds.when.cpus_on.note: What a snapshot file holds, in the question asked before it's loaded: {{label}} is its machine's name, {{when}} when it was taken, {{size}} the file's size, {{count}} its vCPUs.

snapshot-restore.load.holds.cpus_other.note: What a snapshot file holds, in the question asked before it's loaded, when it has no date: {{label}} is its machine's name, {{size}} the file's size, {{count}} its vCPUs.

snapshot-restore.load.holds.when.cpus_ot.message: It holds {{label}} as it was on {{when}} ({{size, bytes}}, {{count}} vCPUs).
snapshot-restore.load.holds.when.cpus_ot.note: What a snapshot file holds, in the question asked before it's loaded: {{label}} is its machine's name, {{when}} when it was taken, {{size}} the file's size, {{count}} its vCPUs.

snapshot-restore.load.holds.note: What a snapshot file holds, in the question asked before it's loaded, when it says neither its date nor its vCPUs: {{label}} is its machine's name, {{size}} the file's size.

snapshot-restore.load.holds.when.message: It holds {{label}} as it was on {{when}} ({{size, bytes}}).
snapshot-restore.load.holds.when.note: What a snapshot file holds, in the question asked before it's loaded, when it doesn't say its vCPUs: {{label}} is its machine's name, {{when}} when it was taken, {{size}} the file's size.

snapshot-restore.load.replaces.running.message: This will power off this machine immediately, like pulling the plug, and the snapshot's machine will take its place, continuing from where it was saved.
snapshot-restore.load.replaces.running.note: What happens to the machine, in the question asked before a snapshot file is loaded while it runs.

snapshot-restore.load.replaces.message: The snapshot's machine will take this machine's place, continuing from where it was saved.
snapshot-restore.load.replaces.note: What happens to the machine, in the question asked before a snapshot file is loaded while it isn't running.

snapshot-restore.load.written.message: Everything written to {{disk}} will be replaced by the snapshot's changes to the disk.
snapshot-restore.load.written.note: What happens to the disk's changes, in the question asked before a snapshot file is loaded; {{disk}} names the disk.

snapshot-restore.load.written.size.message: Everything written to {{disk}} ({{size, bytes}}) will be replaced by the snapshot's changes to the disk.
snapshot-restore.load.written.size.note: What happens to the disk's changes, in the question asked before a snapshot file is loaded; {{disk}} names the disk, {{size}} what it has written.

snapshot-restore.load.title.note: Title of the question asked before a snapshot file is loaded on a test machine.

snapshot-restore.load.ok.note: The confirm button (drawn as a warning) of the question asked before a snapshot file is loaded.

worker-header.otherShape.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (a file, or the machine kept suspended) is refused before anything is touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow) because the machine's settings or disks changed since: the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (snapshots:worker-header.otherShape.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name; {{name}} is the file's name, or “the suspended machine”.

worker-header.otherShape.cause.message: It was taken of a machine with other settings or disks than {{machine}} has now. To use it, create a machine like it on the Home page (Snapshots tab).
worker-header.otherShape.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-header.otherShape, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-header.otherMachine.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (a file, or the machine kept suspended) is refused before anything is touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow) because it is of another test machine: the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (snapshots:worker-header.otherMachine.cause); {{other}} and {{otherId}} are its machine's name and id, {{machine}} and {{id}} the page's; {{name}} is the file's name, or “the suspended machine”.

worker-header.otherMachine.cause.message: It's a snapshot of {{other}} (?machine={{otherId}}), but this is {{machine}} (?machine={{id}}). To load it, open this web app with ?machine={{otherId}} in the address. Start boots {{machine}} normally.
worker-header.otherMachine.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-header.otherMachine, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{other}}, {{otherId}}, {{machine}}, {{id}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-header.devicesUnknown.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (a file, or the machine kept suspended) is refused before anything is touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow) because its devices can't be read: the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (snapshots:worker-header.devicesUnknown.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name; {{name}} is the file's name, or “the suspended machine”.

worker-header.devicesUnknown.cause.message: This version of this web app can't read its list of devices; another version may have made it. Start boots {{machine}} normally.
worker-header.devicesUnknown.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-header.devicesUnknown, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-header.otherDevices.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (a file, or the machine kept suspended) is refused before anything is touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow) because its machine had other devices: the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (snapshots:worker-header.otherDevices.cause); {{kinds}} are its devices, {{here}} the machine's, {{machine}} the machine's name; {{name}} is the file's name, or “the suspended machine”.

worker-header.otherDevices.cause.message: Its machine had other devices ({{kinds}}) than this one ({{here}}). Open this web app as that machine was started, with the same disks and network, or Start {{machine}} normally.
worker-header.otherDevices.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-header.otherDevices, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{kinds}}, {{here}}, {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-header.cpus.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (a file, or the machine kept suspended) is refused before anything is touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow) because its vCPU count can't be read: the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (snapshots:worker-header.cpus.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name; {{name}} is the file's name, or “the suspended machine”.

worker-header.cpus.cause.message: Its vCPU count isn't readable. Start boots {{machine}} normally.
worker-header.cpus.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-header.cpus, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-header.memory.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (a file, or the machine kept suspended) is refused before anything is touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow) because its memory can't be read: the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (snapshots:worker-header.memory.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name; {{name}} is the file's name, or “the suspended machine”.

worker-header.memory.cause.message: Its memory size isn't readable. Start boots {{machine}} normally.
worker-header.memory.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-header.memory, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-header.features.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot (a file, or the machine kept suspended) is refused before anything is touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow) because its processor's features can't be read: the headline; why and what to do are the cause under it (snapshots:worker-header.features.cause); {{machine}} is the machine's name; {{name}} is the file's name, or “the suspended machine”.

worker-header.features.cause.message: This version of this web app can't read its processor's features; another version may have made it. Start boots {{machine}} normally.
worker-header.features.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-header.features, on the line under it in the same place; why and what to do. {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-errors.notRestored.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot failed once its disk's changes were being written (Start and Load snapshot… follow); {{machine}} is the machine's name; why is the detail under it, after its cause (snapshots:worker-errors.notRestored.cause) on the line under the headline.

worker-errors.notRestored.cause.message: The machine didn't start, and its disk may hold part of the snapshot's changes. Start boots {{machine}} normally from what is there. To start over from the disk's image, reset the disk.
worker-errors.notRestored.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-errors.notRestored, on the line under it in the same place; what happened. {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-errors.notLoaded.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot file was refused before anything was touched (Start and Load snapshot… follow); {{machine}} is the machine's name; why is the detail under it, after its cause (snapshots:worker-errors.notLoaded.cause) on the line under the headline.

worker-errors.notLoaded.cause.message: Nothing was changed. The machine isn't running, and its disk is as it was. Start boots {{machine}} normally, and Load snapshot… tries another file.
worker-errors.notLoaded.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-errors.notLoaded, on the line under it in the same place; what happened. {{machine}}: as that entry's note says.

worker-start.phase.checking.note: Line on the boot card and the machine's state in the status bar while a snapshot file is checked before it's loaded.

worker-start.phase.restoring.note: Line on the boot card and the machine's state in the status bar while a snapshot's machine is made.

worker-snapshot.phase.freeing.note: The machine's state in the status bar right before a snapshot or Suspend pauses the machine: the guest hands its free memory over, so the snapshot leaves it out.

worker-snapshot.phase.pausing.note: The machine's state in the status bar when a snapshot or Suspend pauses the machine.

worker-snapshot.phase.writing.note: The machine's state in the status bar while a snapshot is written (a percentage may follow).

worker-stage.phase.copying.message: Copying the snapshot to the file
worker-stage.phase.copying.note: The machine's state in the status bar after a snapshot to a file was written to the browser's storage during the pause, while it is copied into the chosen file, the machine already running on (a percentage may follow).

worker-stage.notCopied.message: The snapshot was taken, but copying it into {{name}} failed: the file has none of it, and nothing of it is left in the browser's storage.
worker-stage.notCopied.note: Error details under “Couldn't save the snapshot” (snapshots:worker-snapshot.notSaved) in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot written to the browser's storage during the pause couldn't be copied into the chosen file afterwards; {{name}} is the file's name; why is the detail under it.

worker-snapshot.phase.finishing.note: The machine's state in the status bar while a snapshot's file is closed, the machine already running on.

worker-snapshot.notRunning.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot reached a machine that had already stopped: the headline; why is the cause under it (snapshots:worker-snapshot.notRunning.cause).

worker-snapshot.notRunning.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-snapshot.notRunning, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything.

worker-snapshot.saving.note: Error in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot is asked while another is written: the headline; why is the cause under it (snapshots:worker-snapshot.saving.cause).

worker-snapshot.saving.cause.message: Another snapshot is already being saved.
worker-snapshot.saving.cause.note: Error details: the cause under the headline snapshots:worker-snapshot.saving, on the line under it in the same place; what happened, and what the user can do if anything.

worker-snapshot.ended.message: The machine stopped before it could be paused.
worker-snapshot.ended.note: Detail under “Couldn't save the snapshot” or “Couldn't suspend the machine” in the message bar (under the toolbar): the machine stopped first.

worker-snapshot.notSaved.note: Error headline in the message bar (under the toolbar) when a snapshot failed (the machine runs on); why is the detail under it.
